newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan group says to finish BOJ law revision soon.
newsitem.headline: Japan group says to finish BOJ law revision soon.

text.p: A government study group discussing revisions of the law governing the Bank of Japan plans to complete reform proposals in late October or early November, the head of the group, Yasuhiko Torii, said on Thursday.

Torii disclosed the timing of the completion of final proposals for the reform of the BOJ at a news conference after a meeting of the special study group, which was set up under Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
At Thursday's meeting, group members said it was important for a central bank to release accurate information to global financial markets.
"It would be desirable that overall revisions of the BOJ law be carried out, rather than revisions of some parts of the law," Torii said.

Hashimoto is expected to draw up a final plan based on the proposals of the study group and the ruling coalition, and to submit relevant legislation to the next ordinary parliamentary session beginning in January.
However, the fate of the revisions depends on the outcome of general elections on October 20, as the study group is a private group set up by Hashimoto.
